content: 1. Operational Links with Senior Health Officials: 2. Communication with Conveyance Operators: Current contact details of conveyance operators (including agents or legal representatives) and communication protocols are maintained. Conveyance operators are also provided with updated contact details of competent authorities. 3. Communication with Travelers: 4. Communication with Service Providers: 5. Assessment of Urgent Events: Documented and tested procedures are in place to assess and respond to urgent public health events within 24 hours. These include communication links among hospitals, clinics, airports, ports, ground crossings, laboratories, and other operational areas. 6. WHO Communication Mechanisms: Regularly updated and tested communication systems are established to handle reports and recommendations from the World Health Organization (WHO) regarding national or international public health events. 7. Inspection and Reporting of Public Health Risks on Conveyances: National legislation, administrative acts, and protocols empower competent authorities to inspect conveyances for public health risks. Guidance documents are available to conveyance operators, outlining reporting requirements and procedures for immediate notification of public health events. 8. Medical and Diagnostic Facilities: On-site facilities include specialized warehouses for medical supplies and records. 9. Vaccination and Prophylaxis Assessment: On-site capabilities are available to assess proof of vaccination and prophylaxis as recommended by WHO, tailored to the epidemiological situation and national requirements. 10. Trained Personnel: Adequate numbers of trained personnel are assigned to handle the volume and complexity of travelers at points of entry. 11. Private Interview Spaces: Hygienic and environmentally safe spaces are designated for private interviews with ill travelers. These spaces are appropriately sized and designed to prevent the spread of infection. 12. Transport of Ill Travelers: Arrangements are in place for the safe and hygienic transport of ill travelers to medical facilities. Transport staff are equipped with personal protective equipment (PPE) and trained in infection control techniques. 13. Inspection of Conveyances: Trained personnel are available to inspect conveyances for public health risks. They are knowledgeable about required health-related documents and public health risks associated with conveyances. 14. They are also knowledgeable about vector control, food safety, water safety, and waste management. 15. Vector and Reservoir Control: Integrated vector control programs are in place, covering passenger terminals, cargo areas, and surrounding areas. Trained personnel monitor and control vectors and reservoirs to mitigate public health risks. 16. Public Health Emergency Contingency Plans: Comprehensive contingency plans are developed and integrated with national and local public health response plans. These plans include clear roles and responsibilities for all sectors involved at points of entry. 17. Training and Drills: Periodic training and drills are conducted to familiarize personnel with contingency plans and their respective roles during public health emergencies. 18. Safe Environment for Travelers: 19. Monitoring of Human Remains: Procedures are in place for the safe handling and transport of human remains, including permits, sanitary treatment, and record-keeping. 20. Specialized Capacities for Points of Entry: Procedures are established for communication and management of suspected communicable diseases on aircraft, ships, and ground transport. These include disinsection, quarantine arrangements, and coordination with relevant authorities. 21. Collaboration with Local Medical and Veterinary Facilities: Arrangements are made with local facilities for the isolation, treatment, and care of affected travelers or animals.
